episode_title: Episode 367: Makin It - Dr. Phil Hampton, Professor of Chemistry at CSU Channel Islands

real_qa.q: What was the founding team size and structure when CSU Channel Islands launched in 2001?
real_qa.r: CSU Channel Islands had 13 founding faculty members, who referred to themselves as the Dirty Baker's Dozen, plus a comparable number of staff supporting human resources, physical plant, and other university operations. The team had to create an entire curriculum catalog for all majors within three to four months, working from August to October 2002, before opening to transfer students in fall of 2002.

real_qa.q: What specific educational background and institutions shaped Dr. Phil Hampton's academic journey?
real_qa.r: Dr. Hampton completed his undergraduate degree at St. Olaf College in Minnesota, earned his Ph.D. from Stanford University, and conducted postdoctoral research at Caltech where he focused on polymer science and materials science. His father was a college chemistry professor, which served as his primary role model for pursuing an academic career.
real_qa.requete: Dr. Phil Hampton Stanford Caltech chemistry education

real_qa.q: How did CSU Channel Islands engage with the community during its founding phase?
real_qa.r: CSU Channel Islands brought community members into the hiring process, with one community member serving as a table participant who provided feedback to the president on faculty selections. The university prioritized outreach to community colleges to inform transfer students about how their coursework would apply toward CSU Channel Islands majors, treating community needs as central to the institution's founding mission.
real_qa.requete: CSU Channel Islands community engagement founding strategy

real_qa.q: How long did it take for CSU Channel Islands to transition from planning to accepting its first students?
real_qa.r: CSU Channel Islands had approximately three to four months to create its complete curriculum catalog from August to October 2002, and opened to transfer students in fall of 2002, which was one year after the founding faculty began in 2001.
real_qa.requete: CSU Channel Islands curriculum development timeline 2001 2002

guest.titre: Professor of Chemistry and Dean of the School of Arts and Sciences
guest.bio_context: Dr. Hampton's father was a college chemistry professor, which inspired his early interest in chemistry. He earned his undergraduate degree from St. Olaf College in Minnesota, completed his Ph.D. at Stanford University, and conducted postdoctoral research at Caltech focusing on polymer science and materials science. He worked as a researcher at the University of New Mexico before joining CSU Channel Islands as one of 13 founding faculty members in 2001, where he has remained for 25 years.
